title: Heap use-after-free via missing return after conditional free in parse_charlie
rationale: Root cause is entry.c:58 -- free(r) inside the conditional block lacks a return, so execution falls through to entry.c:60 which dereferences the freed pointer. Adding return immediately after free(r) terminates the early-free path before the dangling write.
variants_checked: entry.c:parse_alpha -- single free at function end, no conditional-free-without-return pattern. entry.c:parse_bravo -- stack buffer only, no heap allocation, not applicable.
bypass_considered: An attacker tries buf[0]=0xff to trigger the early-free path. With the fix, that path returns immediately after free(r), so line 60 is never reached. Any other value of buf[0] skips the free entirely, so r is live when line 60 executes.
test_note: No regression test added. The canary target has no C test infrastructure.
review_reason: The single-line return after free(r) at line 58 directly fixes the documented root cause -- a missing early exit that lets execution fall through to the use-after-free write at line 60. The hunk is entirely within parse_charlie. No new parsing, input trust, or validation weakening is introduced. The fix is minimal and matches the early-return idiom already used elsewhere in the file.
